data.summary: This 16‑week plan starts with the student’s weak units (6 and 7) in the first half, then cycles through the remaining units, ensuring each unit appears at least once. The final two weeks focus on mixed review and timed practice. Each week is limited to 3 study hours, with concrete tasks that can be completed in a single sitting.

weeks.focus: Begin with Unit 6 – rotational kinetic energy.
tasks: Read the textbook section on 6.1 and write a summary of key equations.
Do 10 practice problems on rotational kinetic energy, then check solutions and note errors.

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of torque and work in rotating systems.
tasks: Solve 8 torque‑work problems from the workbook, marking each with the correct units.
Create a concept map linking torque, work, and energy for rotating systems.
Derive the angular momentum formula for a point mass and verify with a calculator.
Answer 5 free‑response questions on angular momentum conservation.
Work through 7 example problems on conservation of angular momentum.
Write a short explanation of when angular momentum is conserved.
Read the section on 7.1 and list the defining equations.
Solve 6 problems that identify SHM in different systems.
Calculate frequency and period for 5 different oscillators.
Create flashcards for the formulas and key relationships.
Plot displacement vs. time for a simple pendulum using spreadsheet software.
Answer 4 conceptual questions about phase and amplitude.
Derive total energy expression for a mass‑spring system.
Solve 5 problems comparing kinetic and potential energy at different points.
Complete 8 vector addition problems in 1D.
Write a brief summary of scalar vs. vector quantities.
Solve 6 motion‑graph problems, labeling axes and interpreting slopes.
Create a cheat sheet of key kinematic equations.
Draw 4 motion diagrams for different scenarios.
Explain how changing reference frames affects velocity vectors.
Solve 7 projectile motion problems, including range and time of flight.
Summarize the method for decomposing vectors into components.
Take a 60‑minute timed practice test covering all topics.
Review incorrect answers and update a personal error log.
Complete a full-length practice exam under timed conditions.
Analyze pacing and identify any remaining weak spots.
Re‑solve the most challenging problems from weeks 1‑8.
Create a summary sheet of key formulas for quick reference.
Do a 30‑minute mental math warm‑up and review flashcards.
Plan a pre‑exam routine: sleep, breakfast, and travel schedule.

data.final_week_advice: On exam day, arrive early, bring all allowed materials, and use the pacing plan from week 14 to manage time. After the test, take a short walk to decompress before heading home.
